<t0>The Client</t0>
A strong product, an AI "marketing office", and an outbound engine that wasn't producing replies.

<t0>ContentBuilder</t0> is a US AI training platform. It turns a company's existing knowledge (docs, SOPs, recordings, policies) into structured, AI-narrated, multilingual training with full LMS delivery (SCORM/xAPI, SSO/SCIM). Its sister module, <t1>Lumi</t1>, handles HR work: writing job descriptions, posting roles, screening applicants and running first-round interviews.

I came in as Marketing Manager on contract. The company had an AI "marketing office" with departments and agents already set up, but none of it was connected to real platforms like Search Console, GA4, social publishing or Canva. Cold email was going out, but replies weren't coming back.
<t0>01: Deliverability Diagnosis</t0>
The copy wasn't the problem. Microsoft was sending every email to spam.
The easy assumption was bad copy. Before rewriting anything, I ran a full inbox-placement test across every sending mailbox and read all five sub-reports:
<t0>Google → Google: 96% inbox.</t0> Content, SPF, DKIM and DMARC all passed. Spam-filter score 0, no blacklists.
<t0>Google → Microsoft: 0% inbox, 100% spam.</t0> Every email to an Outlook or Microsoft 365 address was landing in junk.

That isolated the failure to <t0>sender reputation with Microsoft</t0>. Content, authentication and blacklisting were all ruled out. For a B2B audience, where a large share of companies run on Microsoft 365, that alone explains most of the missing replies.

The fix plan: register with Microsoft SNDS/JMRP, add 2–3 sending domains on a second provider, cap volume at 25–40 emails per mailbox per day, segment sends by the recipient's mail provider, and turn off open tracking. I also sized what the client's high-volume target would take in reality: about 200 warmed mailboxes across many domains, with a 3–4 week warm-up that can't be skipped or bought.
<t0>02: ICP & Targeting</t0>
Rebuilt the ideal customer, and found one trigger that beats industry or headcount.

<t0>ICP rebuilt from scratch</t0> when the focus moved to the HR product: from HR/L&D directors at 100–2,000-person companies to <t1>owners, founders and COOs at companies with no dedicated HR person</t1>, who feel the hiring pain directly
<t0>The best targeting signal: 5+ open roles posted right now.</t0> It's public, dated and free to find, and it predicts buying intent better than industry or company size
<t0>15 verticals researched, narrowed to 3</t0> for parallel testing: home & field services, home health & senior care, and multi-site salon/restaurant groups with 10+ locations
<t0>Five full ICP + offer pairs</t0> for the core training product, plus a <t1>40-company manual lead-fit review</t1> to check that real leads matched the ICP before any budget went into sending
